1. # UI Frame and Porting Guide
2. 
3. Hero Adventure screens use a shared semantic frame contract. The contract describes
4. what belongs together; each platform decides how those regions look and how much space
5. they receive.
6. 
7. ## Four frames
8. 
9. Every screen declares these four frame IDs, even when one has no controls:
10. 
11. | Frame | Default share | Priority | Responsibility |
12. | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
13. | `status` | 15% | P0 | Persistent orientation: identity, health, money, capacity, and progress |
14. | `scene` | 50% | P0 | The current situation: narration, encounter, result, loot, or decision |
15. | `context` | 20% | P1 | One supporting detail mode: odds, inventory, trader, dungeon, scores, or messages |
16. | `actions` | 15% | P0 | Legal choices, grouped as primary, utility, and navigation |
17. 
18. These are allocation targets, not terminal columns or GUI coordinates. When space is
19. limited, retain `actions`, `scene`, and `status` first. Collapse `context` first. When
20. space is wide, `context` can sit beside `scene` without changing the frame IDs.
21. 
22. The four questions are:
23. 
24. - `status`: How am I doing?
25. - `scene`: What is happening?
26. - `context`: What supporting detail do I need?
27. - `actions`: What can I do?
28. 
29. Do not put a choice in `scene`, a long log in `status`, or all available detail in
30. `context`. Each frame should have one job.
31. 
32. ## JSON screen shape
33. 
34. The old top-level `text`, `lists`, and `buttons` arrays are not part of the new format.
35. Each screen has `frames` and one ordered `controls` collection:
36. 
37. ```json
38. {
39.   "id": "journey",
40.   "title": "Leg {leg}/5: {leg_name}",
41.   "frames": [
42.     {"id": "status", "role": "status", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"},
43.     {"id": "scene", "role": "scene", "ratio": 0.50, "priority": "P0"},
44.     {"id": "context", "role": "context", "ratio": 0.20, "priority": "P1"},
45.     {"id": "actions", "role": "actions", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"}
46.   ],
47.   "controls": [
48.     {
49.       "type": "progressbar",
50.       "id": "hp_bar",
51.       "frame": "status",
52.       "label": "HP",
53.       "value": "{hp}",
54.       "max": "{max_hp}",
55.       "kind": "health",
56.       "thresholds": {"warning": 0.35, "critical": 0.15},
57.       "show_text": true
58.     },
59.     {
60.       "type": "text",
61.       "frame": "scene",
62.       "value": "{event_narration}"
63.     },
64.     {
65.       "type": "button",
66.       "frame": "actions",
67.       "label": "Continue",
68.       "action": "advance_event"
69.     }
70.   ]
71. }
72. ```
73. 
74. `frame` is required on every control. The order of controls is the order within its
75. frame. The frame declaration is the contract; the renderer owns the geometry.
76. 
77. ## Control types
78. 
79. ### `text`
80. 
81. Displays a formatted value in its frame.
82. 
83. ```json
84. {"type": "text", "frame": "scene", "value": "You found a dungeon."}
85. ```
86. 
87. Use `variant: "title"` only for the screen heading. Keep headings in `scene` so menu
88. and event screens have the same title treatment.
89. 
90. ### `input`
91. 
92. Provides editable input. The GUI currently reserves `id: "name_input"` for character
93. creation and binds it to the controller's pending hero name.
94. 
95. ```json
96. {
97.   "type": "input",
98.   "id": "name_input",
99.   "frame": "scene",
100.   "label": "Hero Name:",
101.   "value": "{pending_name}",
102.   "placeholder": "Enter hero name"
103. }
104. ```
105. 
106. ### `list`
107. 
108. Renders rows from a controller context list. Lists belong in `context`, not `scene`.
109. Use `max_rows` for a first-page budget and `overflow: "page"` when the platform
110. supports a detail or paging interaction.
111. 
112. ```json
113. {
114.   "type": "list",
115.   "id": "list_inventory",
116.   "frame": "context",
117.   "label": "Inventory",
118.   "max_rows": 12,
119.   "overflow": "page"
120. }
121. ```
122. 
123. Rows may contain `text`, `action`, and `enabled`. A row with an action is interactive;
124. a disabled row is informational.
125. 
126. ### `button`
127. 
128. Represents an available action and belongs in `actions`.
129. 
130. ```json
131. {
132.   "type": "button",
133.   "frame": "actions",
134.   "label": "Fight ({fight_win_pct}%)",
135.   "action": "fight",
136.   "visible_if": "allow_run"
137. }
138. ```
139. 
140. Renderers should preserve the JSON order and separate primary choices from utility
141. and navigation choices when their platform supports grouping. Do not create a button
142. for an unavailable action.
143. 
144. ### `progressbar`
145. 
146. A progressbar communicates an amount relative to a known maximum. It is not a
147. scrollbar and must never be used to represent document overflow.
148. 
149. Required fields are `id`, `frame`, `label`, `value`, `max`, and `kind`. `value` and
150. `max` may be formatted controller bindings or numeric literals. Keep the numeric
151. text visible even when the platform also shows a visual bar.
152. 
153. Supported kinds currently used by the GUI are:
154. 
155. - `health`: lower values become warning/critical.
156. - `capacity`: higher values become warning/critical and values above max remain
157.   visibly full with a warning color.
158. - `journey`, `dungeon`, `levelup`, and `honor`: neutral progression.
159. - `odds`: comparative action likelihood in combat context.
160. 
161. Renderers clamp only the visual fill to 0-1; they must not alter the displayed values.
162. Reject a zero or negative maximum as invalid screen data.
163. 
164. ## GUI implementation notes
165. 
166. `play_gui.py` creates four weighted rows using the 15/50/20/15 default. The ratios do
167. not live in widget coordinates in JSON. Empty frames collapse rather than leaving a
168. large blank region on menu screens. `scene` and `context` use bounded internal
169. content areas; the root window is not one unbounded scrollable document.
170. 
171. The status frame should stay compact. Prefer one identity line and a few bars over
172. repeating every stat. Context is mode-specific: combat shows odds and enemy facts,
173. inventory shows capacity and item rows, dungeon shows depth, and capital shows
174. affordability or score.
175. 
176. When a control does not fit:
177. 
178. 1. Preserve P0 frames and their primary controls.
179. 2. Collapse or page the P1 context.
180. 3. Shorten or wrap content inside its frame.
181. 4. Add a detail action rather than expanding the whole screen.
182. 
183. Do not solve overflow by adding another permanent frame or by moving controls into
184. an unrelated frame.
185. 
186. ## Porting checklist
187. 
188. 1. Load each screen and validate all four frame IDs, ratios, priorities, and control
189.    frame references.
190. 2. Allocate platform space using the ratios as defaults, then define responsive
191.    reflow for narrow and wide displays.
192. 3. Render controls by type; keep action dispatch and controller bindings unchanged.
193. 4. Give `scene` and `context` bounded overflow behavior appropriate to the platform.
194. 5. Preserve progressbar labels, numeric values, maxima, kinds, and threshold meaning.
195. 6. Keep actions keyboard-addressable in terminal ports and clickable in GUI ports.
196. 7. Test the longest narration, combat context, inventory, trader lists, level-up,
197.    and capital screens at the smallest supported size.
198. 8. Record platform-specific geometry in the renderer or platform guide, not in the
199.    shared JSON.
200. 
201.

+    }

+        height: auto;
+        padding: 0 1;
+    }
+
+    .progress_line {
+        width: 1fr;
+        height: 1;

+        width: 1fr;

+

+        width: 1fr;
+        height: auto;

+        padding: 0 1;

+    .action_button {

+        margin: 0 1;
+    }
+    """

+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.controller = GameController()
+        self.screens = self._load_screens()
+        self.ctx = {}
+        self._button_actions = {}
+        self._button_seq = 0
+
+    def _load_screens(self):
+        ui_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "ui"
+        screens = {}
+        for path in ui_dir.glob("*.json"):
+            data = json.loads(path.read_text())
+            screens[data["id"]] = data
+        return screens
+
+    def _fmt(self, value):
+        return str(value).format_map(SafeDict(self.ctx))
+
+    def _resolve_number(self, value, control_id, field):
+        rendered = self._fmt(value)
+        try:
+            return float(rendered)
+        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Invalid progressbar {field} for {control_id}: {rendered!r}"
+            ) from exc
+
+    def _frame_definitions(self, screen):
+        if len(screen["frames"]) != len(self.FRAME_ORDER):
+            raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} must declare exactly four frames")
+        definitions = {frame["id"]: frame for frame in screen["frames"]}
+        if set(definitions) != set(self.FRAME_ORDER):
+            raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} has invalid frame IDs")
+        ratio_total = sum(float(definitions[frame_id]["ratio"]) for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER)
+        if abs(ratio_total - 1.0) > 0.001:
+            raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} frame ratios must total 1.0")
+        for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
+            frame = definitions[frame_id]
+            expected_ratio = self.FRAME_WEIGHTS[frame_id] / 100
+            if frame.get("role") != frame_id or abs(float(frame["ratio"]) - expected_ratio) > 0.001:
+                raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} has invalid {frame_id} frame metadata")
+        return definitions
+
+    def compose(self) -> ComposeResult:
+        yield Header(show_clock=True)
+        with Vertical(id="layout"):
+            with Vertical(id="frame_status", classes="frame"):
+                yield Vertical(id="status_content", classes="frame_content")
+            with Vertical(id="frame_scene", classes="frame"):
+                yield VerticalScroll(id="scene_content", classes="frame_content")
+            with Vertical(id="frame_context", classes="frame"):
+                yield VerticalScroll(id="context_content", classes="frame_content")
+            with Vertical(id="frame_actions", classes="frame"):
+                yield Vertical(id="actions_content", classes="frame_content")
+        yield Footer()
+
+    async def on_mount(self):
+        await self.refresh_screen()
+
+    def _button_id(self, action):
+        button_id = f"act_{self._button_seq}"
+        self._button_seq += 1
+        self._button_actions[button_id] = action
+        return button_id
+
+    def _progressbar_text(self, control, compact=False):
+        control_id = control["id"]
+        value = self._resolve_number(control["value"], control_id, "value")
+        maximum = self._resolve_number(control["max"], control_id, "max")
+        if maximum <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"Progressbar {control_id} must have a positive max")
+
+        ratio = value / maximum
+        display_ratio = min(1.0, max(0.0, ratio))
+        kind = control.get("kind", "journey")
+        color = self.BAR_COLORS.get(kind, "cyan")
+        thresholds = control.get("thresholds", {})
+        if kind == "health":
+            if ratio <= thresholds.get("critical", 0.15):
+                color = "red"
+            elif ratio <= thresholds.get("warning", 0.35):
+                color = "yellow"
+        elif kind == "capacity":
+            if ratio >= thresholds.get("critical", 1.0):
+                color = "red"
+            elif ratio >= thresholds.get("warning", 0.8):
+                color = "yellow"
+
+        width = 8 if compact else max(12, min(28, (self.size.width - 34) // 2))
+        filled = round(display_ratio * width)
+        bar = "#" * filled + "-" * (width - filled)
+        label = self._fmt(control.get("label", control_id))
+        text = Text()
+        text.append(f"{label:<12} ")
+        text.append(f"[{bar}]", style=color)
+        if control.get("show_text", True):
+            text.append(f" {value:g}/{maximum:g}")
+        return text
+
+    async def _mount_text(self, parent, control, title=False):
+        value = self._fmt(control.get("value", ""))
+        if not value and not control.get("show_empty", False):
+            return
+        if title:
+            value = Text(value, style="bold cyan")
+        await parent.mount(Static(value, classes="line"))
+
+    async def _mount_input(self, parent, control):
+        row = Horizontal(classes="input_row")
+        await parent.mount(row)
+        await row.mount(Label(self._fmt(control.get("label", "")), classes="input_label"))
+        name_input = Input(
+            placeholder=control.get("placeholder", ""),
+            id=control.get("id"),
+        )
+        name_input.value = self.controller.pending_name
+        await row.mount(name_input)
+
+    async def _mount_list(self, parent, control):
+        list_id = control["id"]
+        label = control.get("label")
+        rows = self.ctx.get(list_id, [])
+        if label:
+            await parent.mount(Static(self._fmt(label), classes="list_label"))
+
+        max_rows = control.get("max_rows")
+        visible_rows = rows[:max_rows] if max_rows else rows
+        for row in visible_rows:
+            text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""))
+            action = row.get("action")
+            enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
+            if action and enabled:
+                button_id = self._button_id(action)
+                await parent.mount(Button(text, classes="action_button", id=button_id))
+            else:
+                await parent.mount(Static(f"- {text}", classes="disabled_line"))
+
+        if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
+            await parent.mount(Static(
+                f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; scroll for more.",
+                classes="disabled_line",
+            ))
+
+    async def _mount_button(self, parent, control):
+        visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
+        if visible_if and not self.ctx.get(visible_if):
+            return None
+        label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""))
+        action = control.get("action")
+        if not action:
+            return Static(f"- {label}", classes="disabled_line")
+        button_id = self._button_id(action)
+        return Button(label, classes="action_button", id=button_id)
+
+    async def _mount_regular_control(self, parent, control):
+        control_type = control["type"]
+        if control_type == "text":
+            await self._mount_text(parent, control, title=control.get("variant") == "title")
+        elif control_type == "input":
+            await self._mount_input(parent, control)
+        elif control_type == "progressbar":
+            await parent.mount(Static(
+                self._progressbar_text(control),
+                classes="progress_line",
+            ))
+        elif control_type == "list":
+            await self._mount_list(parent, control)
+        else:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported control type {control_type!r}")
+
+    async def _mount_frame_controls(self, frame_id, parent, controls):
+        if frame_id == "actions":
+            buttons = []
+            for control in controls:
+                if control["type"] != "button":
+                    await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
+                    continue
+                button = await self._mount_button(parent, control)
+                if button is not None:
+                    buttons.append(button)
+            for offset in range(0, len(buttons), 3):
+                row = Horizontal(classes="action_row")
+                await parent.mount(row)
+                for button in buttons[offset:offset + 3]:
+                    await row.mount(button)
+            return
+
+        index = 0
+        while index < len(controls):
+            control = controls[index]
+            if control["type"] == "progressbar" and control.get("compact"):
+                compact = []
+                while index < len(controls):
+                    candidate = controls[index]
+                    if candidate["type"] != "progressbar" or not candidate.get("compact"):
+                        break
+                    compact.append(candidate)
+                    index += 1
+                row = Horizontal(classes="compact_row")
+                await parent.mount(row)
+                for candidate in compact:
+                    await row.mount(Static(
+                        self._progressbar_text(candidate, compact=True),
+                        classes="compact_progress",
+                    ))
+                continue
+            await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
+            index += 1
+
+    async def refresh_screen(self):
+        if self.controller.quit_requested:
+            self.exit()
+            return
+
+        screen_id = self.controller.screen
+        screen = self.screens.get(screen_id)
+        if not screen:
+            self.controller.screen = "front_page"
+            screen = self.screens["front_page"]
+            screen_id = "front_page"
+
+        self._frame_definitions(screen)
+        self.ctx = self.controller.get_context()
+        self._button_actions = {}
+        self._button_seq = 0
+
+        controls_by_frame = {frame_id: [] for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER}
+        for control in screen["controls"]:
+            frame_id = control["frame"]
+            if frame_id not in controls_by_frame:
+                raise ValueError(f"Control uses unknown frame {frame_id!r}")
+            controls_by_frame[frame_id].append(control)
+
+        for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
+            frame = self.query_one(f"#frame_{frame_id}", Vertical)
+            frame.display = bool(controls_by_frame[frame_id])
+            content = self.query_one(f"#{frame_id}_content", (Vertical, VerticalScroll))
+            await content.remove_children()
+            if frame.display:
+                await self._mount_frame_controls(
+                    frame_id,
+                    content,
+                    controls_by_frame[frame_id],
+                )
+
+    async def on_input_submitted(self, event: Input.Submitted):
+        if event.input.id == "name_input":
+            self.controller.set_pending_name(event.value.strip())
+            await self.refresh_screen()
+
+    async def on_button_pressed(self, event: Button.Pressed):
+        action = self._button_actions.get(event.button.id or "")
+        if not action:
+            return
+        if self.controller.screen == "character_creation":
+            name = self.query_one("#name_input", Input).value.strip()
+            self.controller.set_pending_name(name)
+        self.controller.dispatch(action)
+        await self.refresh_screen()
+
+
+def main():
+    HeroAdventureTUI().run()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+compact columns and renders consecutive compact progressbars on one line. Scene and
+context are bounded scrollable regions; status and actions are fixed and must not

import asyncio

import json
from play import HeroAdventureTUI
from hero_engine import HeroAdventureEngine

async def prepare(controller, screen_id):
    controller.engine = HeroAdventureEngine('Tester', 'Hitter')
    controller.ctx = {}
    controller.screen = screen_id
    if screen_id == 'character_creation':
        controller.engine = None
    elif screen_id == 'combat':
        controller._start_combat('Goblin', 'journey')
    elif screen_id in {'dungeon_floor_preview', 'dungeon_boss_preview'}:
        e = controller.engine
        e.in_dungeon = True
        e.dungeon_name = "The Goblin's Den"
        e.dungeon_boss = 'Goblin King'
        e.dungeon_floors = ['Goblin Scavenger', 'Goblin Sentry', 'Goblin Bruiser', 'Goblin Shaman', 'Goblin Champion']
        e.dungeon_event_count = 5 if screen_id == 'dungeon_boss_preview' else 0
        controller._enter_dungeon_floor_preview()
    elif screen_id == 'item_detail':
        item = controller.engine.generate_random_item()
        controller.engine.inventory = [item]
        controller.selected_item_letter = 'a'
    elif screen_id == 'wandering_trader':
        controller.trader_offer = [controller.engine.generate_random_item() for _ in range(5)]
    elif screen_id == 'combat_result':
        controller.ctx = {'result_text': 'Victory!', 'combat_rounds': [{'text': 'A hit.', 'action': None, 'enabled': False}]}
    elif screen_id in {'loot_screen', 'magic_shrine_event'}:
        controller.ctx = {'loot_cash': 25, 'loot_lines': [{'text': 'Common Sword', 'action': None, 'enabled': False}], 'loot_items': []}
    elif screen_id == 'capital_result':
        controller.ctx = {'final_house': 'Cottage', 'final_score': 100, 'final_pension': 100}

async def main():
    app = HeroAdventureTUI()
    async with app.run_test(size=(120, 40)) as pilot:
        screen_ids = sorted(app.screens)
        for screen_id in screen_ids:
            await prepare(app.controller, screen_id)
            await app.refresh_screen()
            await pilot.pause()
            frames = [app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}') for frame_id in app.FRAME_ORDER]
            visible = [frame for frame in frames if frame.display]
            assert all(frame.region.y >= 1 and frame.region.bottom <= 39 for frame in visible), screen_id
            assert all(a.region.bottom <= b.region.y for a, b in zip(visible, visible[1:])), screen_id
            for frame_id in ('status', 'actions'):
                frame = app.query_one(f'#frame_{frame_id}')
                if not frame.display:
                    continue
                for child in app.query_one(f'#{frame_id}_content').children:
                    assert child.region.y >= frame.region.y, (screen_id, frame_id, child.region)
                    assert child.region.bottom <= frame.region.bottom, (screen_id, frame_id, child.region, frame.region)
        print(f'Validated {len(screen_ids)} screens at 120x40; fixed-frame children stayed inside bounds')

asyncio.run(main())

content.text: This is not what I envisaged, the screen is not separated into frames with specific information in the frame, it's the same as before, how did you use 44 credits and 30 minutes to make no visual changes! Describe again to me the default ratios we developed.

You’re right—the implementation preserved the old document-like layout instead of creating visibly distinct information panes.

The agreed default was:

| Frame | Ratio | Priority | Contents |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **Status** | 15% | P0 | Hero identity, HP, gold, carry, journey/dungeon progress, key skills |
| **Scene** | 50% | P0 | Current event, narration, encounter, result, loot, or retirement decision |
| **Context** | 20% | P1 | One supporting mode: combat odds, inventory, dungeon details, trader/capital data, or messages |
| **Actions** | 15% | P0 | Legal actions only: roughly 70% primary, 20% utility, 10% navigation |

These were meant to be four visibly separated, bounded frames—not merely controls tagged with frame names. Under pressure, `context` collapses first; `actions`, `scene`, and `status` remain. On wide screens, context may move beside scene at roughly 25%/75%, but the semantic separation remains.

I have the terminal version, play.py and there is one named frame for the let and everything is just in a bundle at the top, status is muddled up with a ton of other details. The majority of the screen is filled with controls that could have been stack horizontally, but are stacked verticlaly with only 7 lines of text left for everything else, the gui version looks the same.

The failure mode is clear: I treated frame names as routing metadata, but the implementation did not give each frame a strong visual surface or an appropriate layout strategy. I’m re-reading both renderers to map exactly where the status bundle, action controls, and scene area are consuming space before rewriting the plan.

223.     def _progressbar_text(self, control, compact=False):
224.         control_id = control["id"]
225.         value = self._resolve_number(control["value"], control_id, "value")
226.         maximum = self._resolve_number(control["max"], control_id, "max")
227.         if maximum <= 0:
228.             raise ValueError(f"Progressbar {control_id} must have a positive max")
229. 
230.         ratio = value / maximum
231.         display_ratio = min(1.0, max(0.0, ratio))
232.         kind = control.get("kind", "journey")
233.         color = self.BAR_COLORS.get(kind, "cyan")
234.         thresholds = control.get("thresholds", {})
235.         if kind == "health":
236.             if ratio <= thresholds.get("critical", 0.15):
237.                 color = "red"
238.             elif ratio <= thresholds.get("warning", 0.35):
239.                 color = "yellow"
240.         elif kind == "capacity":
241.             if ratio >= thresholds.get("critical", 1.0):
242.                 color = "red"
243.             elif ratio >= thresholds.get("warning", 0.8):
244.                 color = "yellow"
245. 
246.         width = 8 if compact else max(12, min(28, (self.size.width - 34) // 2))
247.         filled = round(display_ratio * width)
248.         bar = "#" * filled + "-" * (width - filled)
249.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", control_id))
250.         text = Text()
251.         text.append(f"{label:<12} ")
252.         text.append(f"[{bar}]", style=color)
253.         if control.get("show_text", True):
254.             text.append(f" {value:g}/{maximum:g}")
255.         return text

292.             else:

294. 
295.         if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
296.             await parent.mount(Static(
297.                 f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; scroll for more.",
298.                 classes="disabled_line",
299.             ))

302.         visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
303.         if visible_if and not self.ctx.get(visible_if):
304.             return None
305.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""))
306.         action = control.get("action")
307.         if not action:
308.             return Static(f"- {label}", classes="disabled_line")
309.         button_id = self._button_id(action)
310.         return Button(label, classes="action_button", id=button_id)

316.         elif control_type == "input":

318.         elif control_type == "progressbar":
319.             await parent.mount(Static(
320.                 self._progressbar_text(control),
321.                 classes="progress_line",
322.             ))
323.         elif control_type == "list":
324.             await self._mount_list(parent, control)
325.         else:

328.     async def _mount_frame_controls(self, frame_id, parent, controls):
329.         if frame_id == "actions":
330.             buttons = []
331.             for control in controls:
332.                 if control["type"] != "button":
333.                     await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
334.                     continue
335.                 button = await self._mount_button(parent, control)
336.                 if button is not None:
337.                     if self.size.width < 100:
338.                         button.add_class("narrow_action")
339.                     buttons.append(button)
340.             columns = 4 if self.size.width >= 80 else 3
341.             for offset in range(0, len(buttons), columns):
342.                 row = Horizontal(classes="action_row")
343.                 if self.size.width < 100:
344.                     row.add_class("narrow_action")
345.                 await parent.mount(row)
346.                 for button in buttons[offset:offset + columns]:
347.                     await row.mount(button)
348.             return
349. 
350.         index = 0
351.         while index < len(controls):
352.             control = controls[index]
353.             if control["type"] == "progressbar" and control.get("compact"):
354.                 compact = []
355.                 while index < len(controls):
356.                     candidate = controls[index]
357.                     if candidate["type"] != "progressbar" or not candidate.get("compact"):
358.                         break
359.                     compact.append(candidate)
360.                     index += 1
361.                 row = Horizontal(classes="compact_row")
362.                 await parent.mount(row)
363.                 for candidate in compact:
364.                     await row.mount(Static(
365.                         self._progressbar_text(candidate, compact=True),
366.                         classes="compact_progress",
367.                     ))
368.                 continue
369.             await self._mount_regular_control(parent, control)
370.             index += 1

393.                 raise ValueError(f"Control uses unknown frame {frame_id!r}")

20.     FRAME_ORDER = ("status", "scene", "context", "actions")
21.     FRAME_WEIGHTS = {
22.         "status": 15,
23.         "scene": 50,
24.         "context": 20,
25.         "actions": 15,
26.     }
27.     ACTION_COLUMNS = 3
28.     BAR_COLORS = {
29.         "health": "#35c759",
30.         "capacity": "#f0ad4e",
31.         "journey": "#4ea1ff",
32.         "dungeon": "#b07cff",
33.         "levelup": "#ffd166",
34.         "honor": "#ff9f43",
35.         "odds": "#69d2a0",
36.     }
37. 
38.     def __init__(self, root):
39.         self.root = root
40.         self.root.title("Hero Adventure")
41.         self.root.geometry("980x760")
42.         self.controller = GameController()
43.         self.screens = self._load_screens()
44.         self.name_var = ctk.StringVar(value="")
45.         self.frame = None
46.         self._action_index = 0
47. 
48.         ctk.set_appearance_mode("dark")
49.         ctk.set_default_color_theme("dark-blue")
50.         self.render()
51. 
52.     def _load_screens(self):
53.         ui_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "ui"
54.         screens = {}
55.         for path in ui_dir.glob("*.json"):
56.             data = json.loads(path.read_text())
57.             screens[data["id"]] = data
58.         return screens
59. 
60.     def _fmt(self, value, ctx):
61.         return str(value).format_map(SafeDict(ctx))
62. 
63.     def _resolve_number(self, value, ctx, control_id, field):
64.         rendered = self._fmt(value, ctx)
65.         try:
66.             return float(rendered)
67.         except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
68.             raise ValueError(
69.                 f"Invalid progressbar {field} for {control_id}: {rendered!r}"
70.             ) from exc
71. 
72.     def _dispatch(self, action):
73.         if not action:
74.             return
75.         if self.controller.screen == "character_creation":
76.             self.controller.set_pending_name(self.name_var.get().strip())
77.         self.controller.dispatch(action)
78.         if self.controller.quit_requested:
79.             self.root.destroy()
80.             return
81.         self.render()
82. 
83.     def _frame_definitions(self, screen):
84.         if len(screen["frames"]) != len(self.FRAME_ORDER):
85.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} must declare exactly four frames")
86.         definitions = {frame["id"]: frame for frame in screen["frames"]}
87.         missing = set(self.FRAME_ORDER) - definitions.keys()
88.         if missing:
89.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} is missing frames: {sorted(missing)}")
90.         ratio_total = sum(float(definitions[frame_id]["ratio"]) for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER)
91.         if abs(ratio_total - 1.0) > 0.001:
92.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} frame ratios must total 1.0")
93.         for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
94.             frame = definitions[frame_id]
95.             expected_ratio = self.FRAME_WEIGHTS[frame_id] / 100
96.             if frame.get("role") != frame_id or abs(float(frame["ratio"]) - expected_ratio) > 0.001:
97.                 raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} has invalid {frame_id} frame metadata")
98.         return definitions
99. 
100.     def _frame_containers(self, screen):
101.         self.frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self.root)
102.         self.frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=12, pady=12)
103.         self.frame.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
104. 
105.         definitions = self._frame_definitions(screen)
106.         controls_by_frame = {frame_id: [] for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER}
107.         for control in screen["controls"]:
108.             frame_id = control["frame"]
109.             if frame_id not in controls_by_frame:
110.                 raise ValueError(
111.                     f"Control {control.get('id', control.get('type'))} uses unknown frame "
112.                     f"{frame_id!r}"
113.                 )
114.             controls_by_frame[frame_id].append(control)
115. 
116.         containers = {}
117.         for row, frame_id in enumerate(self.FRAME_ORDER):
118.             has_controls = bool(controls_by_frame[frame_id])
119.             weight = self.FRAME_WEIGHTS[frame_id] if has_controls else 0
120.             self.frame.grid_rowconfigure(row, weight=weight, minsize=0)
121.             frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self.frame)
122.             frame.grid(row=row, column=0, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=3)
123.             if not has_controls:
124.                 frame.grid_remove()
125.                 continue
126. 
127.             frame.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
128.             if frame_id in ("scene", "context"):
129.                 content = ctk.CTkScrollableFrame(frame, fg_color="transparent")
130.                 content.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=6, pady=4)
131.             elif frame_id == "actions":
132.                 content = ctk.CTkFrame(frame, fg_color="transparent")
133.                 content.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=6, pady=4)
134.                 for column in range(self.ACTION_COLUMNS):
135.                     content.grid_columnconfigure(column, weight=1)
136.             else:
137.                 content = frame
138.             containers[frame_id] = content
139. 
140.         self._action_index = 0
141.         return containers, controls_by_frame, definitions
142. 
143.     def _add_text(self, parent, control, ctx, title=False):
144.         text = self._fmt(control.get("value", ""), ctx)
145.         if not text and not control.get("show_empty", False):
146.             return
147.         font = ctk.CTkFont(size=24 if title else 14, weight="bold" if title else "normal")
148.         ctk.CTkLabel(
149.             parent,
150.             text=text,
151.             font=font,
152.             anchor="w",
153.             justify="left",
154.             wraplength=900,
155.         ).pack(fill="x", pady=(4, 8) if title else (2, 4))
156. 
157.     def _add_input(self, parent, control, ctx):
158.         row = ctk.CTkFrame(parent, fg_color="transparent")
159.         row.pack(fill="x", pady=4)
160.         label = control.get("label")
161.         if label:
162.             ctk.CTkLabel(row, text=self._fmt(label, ctx), width=90).pack(side="left")
163.         if control.get("id") == "name_input":
164.             self.name_var.set(self.controller.pending_name)
165.             ctk.CTkEntry(
166.                 row,
167.                 textvariable=self.name_var,
168.                 placeholder_text=control.get("placeholder", ""),
169.             ).pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True)
170.         else:
171.             entry = ctk.CTkEntry(
172.                 row,
173.                 placeholder_text=control.get("placeholder", ""),
174.             )
175.             entry.insert(0, self._fmt(control.get("value", ""), ctx))
176.             entry.pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True)
177. 
178.     def _add_progressbar(self, parent, control, ctx):
179.         control_id = control["id"]
180.         value = self._resolve_number(control["value"], ctx, control_id, "value")
181.         maximum = self._resolve_number(control["max"], ctx, control_id, "max")
182.         if maximum <= 0:
183.             raise ValueError(f"Progressbar {control_id} must have a positive max")
184. 
185.         ratio = value / maximum
186.         display_ratio = min(1.0, max(0.0, ratio))
187.         kind = control.get("kind", "neutral")
188.         color = self.BAR_COLORS.get(kind, "#4ea1ff")
189.         thresholds = control.get("thresholds", {})
190.         if kind == "health":
191.             if ratio <= thresholds.get("critical", 0.15):
192.                 color = "#ff4d4d"
193.             elif ratio <= thresholds.get("warning", 0.35):
194.                 color = "#f0ad4e"
195.         elif kind == "capacity":
196.             if ratio >= thresholds.get("critical", 1.0):
197.                 color = "#ff4d4d"
198.             elif ratio >= thresholds.get("warning", 0.8):
199.                 color = "#f0ad4e"
200. 
201.         row = ctk.CTkFrame(parent, fg_color="transparent")
202.         row.pack(fill="x", pady=2)
203.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", control_id), ctx)
204.         text = f"{label}: {value:g}/{maximum:g}" if control.get("show_text", True) else label
205.         ctk.CTkLabel(row, text=text, width=150, anchor="w").pack(side="left")
206.         bar = ctk.CTkProgressBar(row, progress_color=color)
207.         bar.set(display_ratio)
208.         bar.pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True, padx=(6, 0))
209. 
210.     def _add_list(self, parent, control, ctx):
211.         list_id = control["id"]
212.         label = control.get("label")
213.         rows = ctx.get(list_id, [])
214.         if label:
215.             ctk.CTkLabel(
216.                 parent,
217.                 text=self._fmt(label, ctx),
218.                 font=ctk.CTkFont(size=15, weight="bold"),
219.                 anchor="w",
220.             ).pack(anchor="w", pady=(6, 4))
221. 
222.         max_rows = control.get("max_rows")
223.         visible_rows = rows[:max_rows] if max_rows else rows
224.         for row in visible_rows:
225.             text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""), ctx)
226.             action = row.get("action")
227.             enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
228.             if action and enabled:
229.                 ctk.CTkButton(
230.                     parent,
231.                     text=text,
232.                     command=lambda a=action: self._dispatch(a),
233.                     anchor="w",
234.                     height=32,
235.                 ).pack(fill="x", pady=2)
236.             else:
237.                 ctk.CTkLabel(
238.                     parent,
239.                     text=text,
240.                     anchor="w",
241.                     justify="left",
242.                     wraplength=900,
243.                 ).pack(fill="x", pady=2)
244. 
245.         if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
246.             ctk.CTkLabel(
247.                 parent,
248.                 text=f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; open detail to continue.",
249.                 text_color="#aaaaaa",
250.                 anchor="w",
251.             ).pack(fill="x", pady=4)
252. 
253.     def _add_button(self, parent, control, ctx):
254.         visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
255.         if visible_if and not ctx.get(visible_if):
256.             return
257.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""), ctx)
258.         action = control.get("action")
259.         ctk.CTkButton(
260.             parent,
261.             text=label,
262.             command=(lambda a=action: self._dispatch(a)) if action else None,
263.             height=30,
264.         ).grid(
265.             row=self._action_index // self.ACTION_COLUMNS,
266.             column=self._action_index % self.ACTION_COLUMNS,
267.             sticky="ew",
268.             padx=3,
269.             pady=2,
270.         )
271.         self._action_index += 1
272. 
273.     def _render_control(self, parent, control, ctx, screen_id):
274.         control_type = control["type"]
275.         if control_type == "text":
276.             self._add_text(parent, control, ctx, title=control.get("variant") == "title")
277.         elif control_type == "input":
278.             self._add_input(parent, control, ctx)
279.         elif control_type == "progressbar":
280.             self._add_progressbar(parent, control, ctx)
281.         elif control_type == "list":
282.             self._add_list(parent, control, ctx)
283.         elif control_type == "button":
284.             self._add_button(parent, control, ctx)
285.         else:
286.             raise ValueError(
287.                 f"Unsupported control type {control_type!r} on screen {screen_id}"
288.             )
289. 
290.     def render(self):
291.         if self.frame is not None:
292.             self.frame.destroy()
293. 
294.         screen_id = self.controller.screen
295.         screen = self.screens.get(screen_id)
296.         if not screen:
297.             self.controller.screen = "front_page"
298.             screen = self.screens["front_page"]
299. 
300.         ctx = self.controller.get_context()
301.         containers, controls_by_frame, _definitions = self._frame_containers(screen)
302.         for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
303.             parent = containers.get(frame_id)
304.             if parent is None:
305.                 continue
306.             controls = controls_by_frame[frame_id]
307.             for control in controls:
308.                 self._render_control(parent, control, ctx, screen_id)
309. 
310. 
311. def main():
312.     root = ctk.CTk()
313.     DeclarativeGUI(root)
314.     root.mainloop()
315. 
316. 
317. if __name__ == "__main__":
318.     main()

1. # UI Frame and Porting Guide
2. 
3. Hero Adventure screens use a shared semantic frame contract. The contract describes
4. what belongs together; each platform decides how those regions look and how much space
5. they receive.
6. 
7. ## Four frames
8. 
9. Every screen declares these four frame IDs, even when one has no controls:
10. 
11. | Frame | Default share | Priority | Responsibility |
12. | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
13. | `status` | 15% | P0 | Persistent orientation: identity, health, money, capacity, and progress |
14. | `scene` | 50% | P0 | The current situation: narration, encounter, result, loot, or decision |
15. | `context` | 20% | P1 | One supporting detail mode: odds, inventory, trader, dungeon, scores, or messages |
16. | `actions` | 15% | P0 | Legal choices, grouped as primary, utility, and navigation |
17. 
18. These are allocation targets, not terminal columns or GUI coordinates. When space is
19. limited, retain `actions`, `scene`, and `status` first. Collapse `context` first. When
20. space is wide, `context` can sit beside `scene` without changing the frame IDs.
21. 
22. The four questions are:
23. 
24. - `status`: How am I doing?
25. - `scene`: What is happening?
26. - `context`: What supporting detail do I need?
27. - `actions`: What can I do?
28. 
29. Do not put a choice in `scene`, a long log in `status`, or all available detail in
30. `context`. Each frame should have one job.
31. 
32. ## JSON screen shape
33. 
34. The old top-level `text`, `lists`, and `buttons` arrays are not part of the new format.
35. Each screen has `frames` and one ordered `controls` collection:
36. 
37. ```json
38. {
39.   "id": "journey",
40.   "title": "Leg {leg}/5: {leg_name}",
41.   "frames": [
42.     {"id": "status", "role": "status", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"},
43.     {"id": "scene", "role": "scene", "ratio": 0.50, "priority": "P0"},
44.     {"id": "context", "role": "context", "ratio": 0.20, "priority": "P1"},
45.     {"id": "actions", "role": "actions", "ratio": 0.15, "priority": "P0"}
46.   ],
47.   "controls": [
48.     {
49.       "type": "progressbar",
50.       "id": "hp_bar",
51.       "frame": "status",
52.       "label": "HP",
53.       "value": "{hp}",
54.       "max": "{max_hp}",
55.       "kind": "health",
56.       "thresholds": {"warning": 0.35, "critical": 0.15},
57.       "show_text": true
58.     },
59.     {
60.       "type": "text",
61.       "frame": "scene",
62.       "value": "{event_narration}"
63.     },
64.     {
65.       "type": "button",
66.       "frame": "actions",
67.       "label": "Continue",
68.       "action": "advance_event"
69.     }
70.   ]
71. }
72. ```
73. 
74. `frame` is required on every control. The order of controls is the order within its
75. frame. The frame declaration is the contract; the renderer owns the geometry.
76. 
77. Controls may also declare `compact: true` when a renderer can safely place several
78. small controls on one line. The terminal uses this for the persistent status bars and
79. combat odds; a GUI may ignore the hint and give each control its own row.
80. 
81. ## Control types
82. 
83. ### `text`
84. 
85. Displays a formatted value in its frame.
86. 
87. ```json
88. {"type": "text", "frame": "scene", "value": "You found a dungeon."}
89. ```
90. 
91. Use `variant: "title"` only for the screen heading. Keep headings in `scene` so menu
92. and event screens have the same title treatment.
93. 
94. ### `input`
95. 
96. Provides editable input. The GUI currently reserves `id: "name_input"` for character
97. creation and binds it to the controller's pending hero name.
98. 
99. ```json
100. {
101.   "type": "input",
102.   "id": "name_input",
103.   "frame": "scene",
104.   "label": "Hero Name:",
105.   "value": "{pending_name}",
106.   "placeholder": "Enter hero name"
107. }
108. ```
109. 
110. ### `list`
111. 
112. Renders rows from a controller context list. Lists belong in `context`, not `scene`.
113. Use `max_rows` for a first-page budget and `overflow: "page"` when the platform
114. supports a detail or paging interaction.
115. 
116. ```json
117. {
118.   "type": "list",
119.   "id": "list_inventory",
120.   "frame": "context",
121.   "label": "Inventory",
122.   "max_rows": 12,
123.   "overflow": "page"
124. }
125. ```
126. 
127. Rows may contain `text`, `action`, and `enabled`. A row with an action is interactive;
128. a disabled row is informational.
129. 
130. ### `button`
131. 
132. Represents an available action and belongs in `actions`.
133. 
134. ```json
135. {
136.   "type": "button",
137.   "frame": "actions",
138.   "label": "Fight ({fight_win_pct}%)",
139.   "action": "fight",
140.   "visible_if": "allow_run"
141. }
142. ```
143. 
144. Renderers should preserve the JSON order and separate primary choices from utility
145. and navigation choices when their platform supports grouping. Do not create a button
146. for an unavailable action.
147. 
148. ### `progressbar`
149. 
150. A progressbar communicates an amount relative to a known maximum. It is not a
151. scrollbar and must never be used to represent document overflow.
152. 
153. Required fields are `id`, `frame`, `label`, `value`, `max`, and `kind`. `value` and
154. `max` may be formatted controller bindings or numeric literals. Keep the numeric
155. text visible even when the platform also shows a visual bar.
156. 
157. Supported kinds currently used by the GUI are:
158. 
159. - `health`: lower values become warning/critical.
160. - `capacity`: higher values become warning/critical and values above max remain
161.   visibly full with a warning color.
162. - `journey`, `dungeon`, `levelup`, and `honor`: neutral progression.
163. - `odds`: comparative action likelihood in combat context.
164. 
165. Renderers clamp only the visual fill to 0-1; they must not alter the displayed values.
166. Reject a zero or negative maximum as invalid screen data.
167. 
168. ## GUI implementation notes
169. 
170. `play_gui.py` creates four weighted rows using the 15/50/20/15 default. The ratios do
171. not live in widget coordinates in JSON. Empty frames collapse rather than leaving a
172. large blank region on menu screens. `scene` and `context` use bounded internal
173. content areas; the root window is not one unbounded scrollable document.
174. 
175. `play.py` uses the same four rows. At a 120-column terminal it puts actions in four
176. compact columns and renders consecutive compact progressbars on one line. Below 100
177. columns it switches to one-line action controls. Scene and context are bounded
178. scrollable regions; status and actions are fixed and must not overflow their frame.
179. 
180. The status frame should stay compact. Prefer one identity line and a few bars over
181. repeating every stat. Context is mode-specific: combat shows odds and enemy facts,
182. inventory shows capacity and item rows, dungeon shows depth, and capital shows
183. affordability or score.
184. 
185. When a control does not fit:
186. 
187. 1. Preserve P0 frames and their primary controls.
188. 2. Collapse or page the P1 context.
189. 3. Shorten or wrap content inside its frame.
190. 4. Add a detail action rather than expanding the whole screen.
191. 
192. Do not solve overflow by adding another permanent frame or by moving controls into
193. an unrelated frame.
194. 
195. ## Porting checklist
196. 
197. 1. Load each screen and validate all four frame IDs, ratios, priorities, and control
198.    frame references.
199. 2. Allocate platform space using the ratios as defaults, then define responsive
200.    reflow for narrow and wide displays.
201. 3. Render controls by type; keep action dispatch and controller bindings unchanged.
202. 4. Give `scene` and `context` bounded overflow behavior appropriate to the platform.
203. 5. Preserve progressbar labels, numeric values, maxima, kinds, and threshold meaning.
204. 6. Keep actions keyboard-addressable in terminal ports and clickable in GUI ports.
205. 7. Test the longest narration, combat context, inventory, trader lists, level-up,
206.    and capital screens at 80x24 and 120x40 or the platform's equivalent normal sizes.
207. 8. Record platform-specific geometry in the renderer or platform guide, not in the
208.    shared JSON.
209.

1. # Fixed UI frame design for Hero Adventure
2. 
3. ## Problem and proposed approach
4. 
5. The current JSON describes screens as an ordered list of text, lists, and buttons. Both
6. renderers turn that list into an unbounded vertical document, so long narration, combat
7. logs, inventory rows, and action labels compete for height and produce inconsistent
8. layouts. The next UI contract should describe a small set of semantic frames and typed
9. content slots. A GUI or terminal implementation owns actual dimensions, typography, and
10. whether a frame is visible; the shared JSON owns frame identity, role, content binding,
11. priority, and overflow behavior.
12. 
13. The common contract should support exactly four semantic frames:
14. 
15. - `status`: persistent hero identity, HP, gold, carry weight, journey progress, and
16.   only the most important skill/equipment summary.
17. - `scene`: the current event, narration, encounter, preview, result, loot, or
18.   retirement decision. This is the only frame allowed to own the active situation.
19. - `context`: bounded supporting information such as combat odds, inventory rows,
20.   character detail, trader stock, dungeon depth, house affordability, or recent
21.   messages. It shows one context mode at a time rather than every available fact.
22. - `actions`: currently legal choices, ordered into primary, utility, and navigation
23.   groups with stable action identifiers.
24. 
25. `bars` are typed value/max indicators with a semantic label, thresholds, and optional
26. text fallback. A bar is an amount visualization, never a scrollbar.
27. 
28. Every slot should carry enough metadata for implementations to make safe decisions:
29. `role`, `content_type`, `bind`, `priority`, `visible_if`, and `overflow` (`truncate`,
30. `page`, `collapse`, or `replace`). The base should not contain pixel widths, terminal
31. columns, or GUI coordinates.
32. 
33. ## Information inventory from the current game
34. 
35. The journey is the primary persistent view: leg and route, event 0-20, dungeon count,
36. current narration, HP/max HP, gold, eight effective skills, carry/max weight, equipment,
37. save status, and navigation to character/inventory/save/quit. Combat adds enemy
38. fight/defence/magic, action success percentages and risk bands, projected damage and
39. rounds, plus fight/sneak/steal/stealth-kill/run actions. Other screens add bounded
40. lists:
41. inventory/equipment, character stats, item detail, level-up selections (3), dungeon
42. floor/boss preview, trader buy/sell, loot, house affordability and score, high scores,
43. and short event/result messages.
44. 
45. The current `VerticalScroll`/`CTkScrollableFrame` renderers are the direct source of the
46. problem: they make every JSON line and row a full-width vertical widget. Combat rounds
47. and inventory/trader rows therefore need explicit bounded regions in the new contract.
48. 
49. ## Four-frame contract and allocation
50. 
51. The canonical default is a full-width vertical stack. The percentages are allocation
52. targets, not pixel or terminal dimensions:
53. 
54. | Frame | Default share | Importance | Content budget |
55. | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
56. | `status` | 15% of height | P0: always retain | Hero identity, HP/gold/carry bars, journey/dungeon progress, and up to four key skills. |
57. | `scene` | 50% of height | P0: always retain | One active situation: narration plus encounter, result, loot, or retirement choice. |
58. | `context` | 20% of height | P1: retain when useful | One bounded mode: combat odds, inventory/detail, trader, dungeon, score, or recent messages. |
59. | `actions` | 15% of height | P0: always retain | Legal actions only: approximately 70% primary, 20% utility, 10% navigation. |
60. 
61. The `scene` owns the player's current question ("what is happening?"); `actions` owns
62. the answer ("what can I do?"); `status` owns persistent orientation ("how am I doing?");
63. and `context` owns optional explanation ("what supporting detail do I need?"). This
64. prevents narration, tables, and buttons from competing for the same unstructured list.
65. 
66. When space is constrained, preserve frames in this order: `actions`, `scene`, `status`,
67. then `context` only if it still fits. The first three may be compressed but are not
68. silently removed. `context` may collapse to a command or detail view. When space is
69. wide, `context` may move beside `scene` (target 25% of width) while `scene` receives
70. 75%; the semantic frame IDs and content budgets do not change.
71. 
72. `context` must use a single active mode:
73. 
74. - Journey/combat: combat odds and the most relevant enemy facts.
75. - Inventory/character: capacity, equipment, or one selected item.
76. - Dungeon: floor/depth and next threat.
77. - Trader/capital: prices, affordability, pension, or score.
78. - Results/events: a bounded recent-message window, with older text paged or opened.
79. 
80. This gives every implementation the same four decisions while allowing terminal and
81. GUI ports to stack, split, collapse, or omit the context presentation.
82. 
83. ## Bar vocabulary
84. 
85. Bars should be declarative records, for example:
86. 
87. ```json
88. {
89.   "id": "hp",
90.   "label": "HP",
91.   "value": "{hp}",
92.   "max": "{max_hp}",
93.   "kind": "health",
94.   "thresholds": {"warning": 0.35, "critical": 0.15},
95.   "show_text": true
96. }
97. ```
98. 
99. Recommended initial bars:
100. 
101. - `hp`: health/max health; critical and warning thresholds.
102. - `carry`: total weight/max weight; warning near capacity and critical when
103.   overburdened.
104. - `journey`: event/20, or a normalized five-leg journey progress value.
105. - `dungeon`: current floor/6 when inside a dungeon.
106. - `level_up`: selected/3 during level-up.
107. - `honor`: honor marks/15 on character detail, not necessarily persistent HUD.
108. - Combat action odds can use small comparative bars, but only in the combat context
109.   block; they should not replace the clear percentage text.
110. 
111. Cash, score, and house affordability are better represented as labeled values or
112. comparative progress against the selected house cost, because their upper bound is
113. screen-dependent.
114. 
115. ## Recommended shared JSON shape
116. 
117. The later implementation should migrate from `text`/`lists`/`buttons` to a structure
118. similar to:
119. 
120. ```json
121. {
122.   "id": "journey",
123.   "frames": [
124.     {"id": "status", "role": "status", "priority": "P0",
125.      "content": ["hero", "bars", "key_skills"]},
126.     {"id": "scene", "role": "scene", "priority": "P0",
127.      "content": ["narration", "active_situation"]},
128.     {"id": "context", "role": "context", "priority": "P1",
129.      "content": ["active_context"], "overflow": "page"},
130.     {"id": "actions", "role": "actions", "priority": "P0",
131.      "content": ["primary_actions", "utility", "navigation"]}
132.   ]
133. }
134. ```
135. 
136. This is a semantic contract, not a mandate that every implementation render four
137. rectangles in the same geometry. A port may stack or split them, and may collapse the
138. `context` frame, but it must preserve the four roles and their priority rules.
139. 
140. ## Current implementation plan: GUI-first frame migration
141. 
142. This phase deliberately makes a one-way migration. The old `text`/`lists`/`buttons`
143. shape will not be supported and no compatibility adapter will be added. The terminal
144. renderer is a later port and will be expected to consume the new contract.
145. 
146. 1. Define the new screen schema in the UI JSON:
147.    - `frames` declares the four roles and their ratio/priority metadata.
148.    - `controls` is a single ordered collection; every control explicitly declares
149.      `frame`, `type`, and its content binding.
150.    - Use `type: "text"`, `type: "list"`, `type: "button"`, `type: "input"`, and
151.      `type: "progressbar"` rather than implicit top-level arrays.
152.    - `progressbar` controls bind `value` and `max`, expose `kind`, thresholds, and
153.      `show_text`, and remain distinct from scrolling.
154. 2. Migrate all `ui/*.json` screens to the new shape. Put persistent HP, carry, and
155.    journey/dungeon progress bars in `status`; narration and the active event in
156.    `scene`; one bounded list/detail/message mode in `context`; and all choices in
157.    `actions`. Empty frames remain declared so every screen has the same contract.
158. 3. Replace the GUI's single scrollable document with a four-row weighted layout:
159.    `status` 15%, `scene` 50%, `context` 20%, `actions` 15%. Keep frame geometry in
160.    `play_gui.py`, not JSON. Use bounded internal content areas, priority-aware
161.    omission, and explicit rendering for each control type.
162. 4. Add GUI progressbar rendering with `CTkProgressBar`, formatted value/max labels,
163.    clamping for display-only ratios, and semantic colors for health, capacity,
164.    journey, dungeon, level-up, honor, and contextual odds.
165. 5. Handle GUI-only controls such as character-name input through the same frame
166.    dispatch path rather than a screen-specific append to the old vertical document.
167. 6. Write `UI_FRAME_PORTING_GUIDE.md` beside the game documentation. It will describe
168.    the schema, the four-frame ratios and priority rules, control rendering contracts,
169.    overflow behavior, responsive reflow, progressbar semantics, and a porting checklist
170.    for terminal and other platforms.
171. 7. Validate JSON parsing for every screen, compile the GUI module, and exercise the
172.    renderer with representative journey, combat, inventory, trader, level-up, and
173.    capital contexts. Record any frame-capacity lessons in the guide instead of adding
174.    renderer-specific rules to JSON.
175. 
176. ## Implementation progress
177. 
178. The terminal renderer has now been ported to the same schema. At 120x40 it uses four
179. action columns and compact consecutive progressbars; below 100 columns it uses
180. one-line action controls and still keeps fixed status/actions content inside its
181. frame. Scene and context remain bounded scrollable regions for lists that cannot fit
182. simultaneously. All 28 screens have been exercised at 80x24 and 120x40 with
183. representative controller contexts, including journey, combat, inventory, dungeon,
184. level-up, and capital states.
185.

327.         rows = self.ctx.get(list_id, [])
328.         if label:
329.             await parent.mount(Static(self._fmt(label), classes="list_label"))
330. 
331.         max_rows = control.get("max_rows")
332.         visible_rows = rows[:max_rows] if max_rows else rows
333.         for row in visible_rows:
334.             text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""))
335.             action = row.get("action")
336.             enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
337.             if action and enabled:
338.                 button_id = self._button_id(action)
339.                 await parent.mount(Button(text, classes="action_button", id=button_id))
340.             else:
341.                 await parent.mount(Static(f"- {text}", classes="disabled_line"))
342. 
343.         if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
344.             await parent.mount(Static(
345.                 f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; scroll for more.",
346.                 classes="disabled_line",
347.             ))
348. 
349.     async def _mount_button(self, parent, control):
350.         visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
351.         if visible_if and not self.ctx.get(visible_if):
352.             return None
353.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""))
354.         action = control.get("action")
355.         if not action:
356.             return Static(f"- {label}", classes="disabled_line")
357.         button_id = self._button_id(action)
358.         return Button(label, classes="action_button", id=button_id)
359. 
360.     async def _mount_regular_control(self, parent, control):
361.         control_type = control["type"]
362.         if control_type == "text":
363.             await self._mount_text(parent, control, title=control.get("variant") == "title")
364.         elif control_type == "input":
365.             await self._mount_input(parent, control)
366.         elif control_type == "progressbar":
367.             await parent.mount(Static(
368.                 self._progressbar_text(control),
369.                 classes="progress_line",
370.             ))
371.         elif control_type == "list":
372.             await self._mount_list(parent, control)
373.         else:
374.             raise ValueError(f"Unsupported control type {control_type!r}")
375. 
376.     async def _mount_frame_controls(self, frame_id, parent, controls):
377.         if frame_id == "status":
378.             identity = Vertical(classes="status_identity")
379.             bars = Horizontal(classes="status_bars")
380.             await parent.mount(identity)
381.             await parent.mount(bars)
382.             for control in controls:
383.                 target = bars if control["type"] == "progressbar" else identity
384.                 if control["type"] == "progressbar":
385.                     await target.mount(Static(
386.                         self._progressbar_text(control, compact=True),
387.                         classes="compact_progress status_bar",
388.                     ))
389.                 else:
390.                     await self._mount_regular_control(target, control)

1. #!/usr/bin/env python3
2. """CustomTkinter renderer for the four-frame declarative UI."""
3. 
4. from __future__ import annotations
5. 
6. import json
7. from pathlib import Path
8. 
9. import customtkinter as ctk
10. 
11. from hero_engine import GameController
12. 
13. 
14. class SafeDict(dict):
15.     def __missing__(self, key):
16.         return "{" + key + "}"
17. 
18. 
19. class DeclarativeGUI:
20.     FRAME_ORDER = ("status", "scene", "context", "actions")
21.     FRAME_WEIGHTS = {
22.         "status": 15,
23.         "scene": 50,
24.         "context": 20,
25.         "actions": 15,
26.     }
27.     ACTION_COLUMNS = 3
28.     BAR_COLORS = {
29.         "health": "#35c759",
30.         "capacity": "#f0ad4e",
31.         "journey": "#4ea1ff",
32.         "dungeon": "#b07cff",
33.         "levelup": "#ffd166",
34.         "honor": "#ff9f43",
35.         "odds": "#69d2a0",
36.     }
37. 
38.     def __init__(self, root):
39.         self.root = root
40.         self.root.title("Hero Adventure")
41.         self.root.geometry("980x760")
42.         self.controller = GameController()
43.         self.screens = self._load_screens()
44.         self.name_var = ctk.StringVar(value="")
45.         self.frame = None
46.         self._action_index = 0
47. 
48.         ctk.set_appearance_mode("dark")
49.         ctk.set_default_color_theme("dark-blue")
50.         self.render()
51. 
52.     def _load_screens(self):
53.         ui_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "ui"
54.         screens = {}
55.         for path in ui_dir.glob("*.json"):
56.             data = json.loads(path.read_text())
57.             screens[data["id"]] = data
58.         return screens
59. 
60.     def _fmt(self, value, ctx):
61.         return str(value).format_map(SafeDict(ctx))
62. 
63.     def _resolve_number(self, value, ctx, control_id, field):
64.         rendered = self._fmt(value, ctx)
65.         try:
66.             return float(rendered)
67.         except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
68.             raise ValueError(
69.                 f"Invalid progressbar {field} for {control_id}: {rendered!r}"
70.             ) from exc
71. 
72.     def _dispatch(self, action):
73.         if not action:
74.             return
75.         if self.controller.screen == "character_creation":
76.             self.controller.set_pending_name(self.name_var.get().strip())
77.         self.controller.dispatch(action)
78.         if self.controller.quit_requested:
79.             self.root.destroy()
80.             return
81.         self.render()
82. 
83.     def _frame_definitions(self, screen):
84.         if len(screen["frames"]) != len(self.FRAME_ORDER):
85.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} must declare exactly four frames")
86.         definitions = {frame["id"]: frame for frame in screen["frames"]}
87.         missing = set(self.FRAME_ORDER) - definitions.keys()
88.         if missing:
89.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} is missing frames: {sorted(missing)}")
90.         ratio_total = sum(float(definitions[frame_id]["ratio"]) for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER)
91.         if abs(ratio_total - 1.0) > 0.001:
92.             raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} frame ratios must total 1.0")
93.         for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
94.             frame = definitions[frame_id]
95.             expected_ratio = self.FRAME_WEIGHTS[frame_id] / 100
96.             if frame.get("role") != frame_id or abs(float(frame["ratio"]) - expected_ratio) > 0.001:
97.                 raise ValueError(f"Screen {screen['id']} has invalid {frame_id} frame metadata")
98.         return definitions
99. 
100.     def _frame_containers(self, screen):
101.         self.frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self.root)
102.         self.frame.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=12, pady=12)
103.         self.frame.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
104. 
105.         definitions = self._frame_definitions(screen)
106.         controls_by_frame = {frame_id: [] for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER}
107.         for control in screen["controls"]:
108.             frame_id = control["frame"]
109.             if frame_id not in controls_by_frame:
110.                 raise ValueError(
111.                     f"Control {control.get('id', control.get('type'))} uses unknown frame "
112.                     f"{frame_id!r}"
113.                 )
114.             controls_by_frame[frame_id].append(control)
115. 
116.         containers = {}
117.         for row, frame_id in enumerate(self.FRAME_ORDER):
118.             has_controls = bool(controls_by_frame[frame_id])
119.             weight = self.FRAME_WEIGHTS[frame_id] if has_controls else 0
120.             self.frame.grid_rowconfigure(row, weight=weight, minsize=0)
121.             frame = ctk.CTkFrame(self.frame)
122.             frame.grid(row=row, column=0, sticky="nsew", padx=4, pady=3)
123.             if not has_controls:
124.                 frame.grid_remove()
125.                 continue
126. 
127.             frame.grid_columnconfigure(0, weight=1)
128.             if frame_id in ("scene", "context"):
129.                 content = ctk.CTkScrollableFrame(frame, fg_color="transparent")
130.                 content.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=6, pady=4)
131.             elif frame_id == "actions":
132.                 content = ctk.CTkFrame(frame, fg_color="transparent")
133.                 content.pack(fill="both", expand=True, padx=6, pady=4)
134.                 for column in range(self.ACTION_COLUMNS):
135.                     content.grid_columnconfigure(column, weight=1)
136.             else:
137.                 content = frame
138.             containers[frame_id] = content
139. 
140.         self._action_index = 0
141.         return containers, controls_by_frame, definitions
142. 
143.     def _add_text(self, parent, control, ctx, title=False):
144.         text = self._fmt(control.get("value", ""), ctx)
145.         if not text and not control.get("show_empty", False):
146.             return
147.         font = ctk.CTkFont(size=24 if title else 14, weight="bold" if title else "normal")
148.         ctk.CTkLabel(
149.             parent,
150.             text=text,
151.             font=font,
152.             anchor="w",
153.             justify="left",
154.             wraplength=900,
155.         ).pack(fill="x", pady=(4, 8) if title else (2, 4))
156. 
157.     def _add_input(self, parent, control, ctx):
158.         row = ctk.CTkFrame(parent, fg_color="transparent")
159.         row.pack(fill="x", pady=4)
160.         label = control.get("label")
161.         if label:
162.             ctk.CTkLabel(row, text=self._fmt(label, ctx), width=90).pack(side="left")
163.         if control.get("id") == "name_input":
164.             self.name_var.set(self.controller.pending_name)
165.             ctk.CTkEntry(
166.                 row,
167.                 textvariable=self.name_var,
168.                 placeholder_text=control.get("placeholder", ""),
169.             ).pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True)
170.         else:
171.             entry = ctk.CTkEntry(
172.                 row,
173.                 placeholder_text=control.get("placeholder", ""),
174.             )
175.             entry.insert(0, self._fmt(control.get("value", ""), ctx))
176.             entry.pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True)
177. 
178.     def _add_progressbar(self, parent, control, ctx):
179.         control_id = control["id"]
180.         value = self._resolve_number(control["value"], ctx, control_id, "value")
181.         maximum = self._resolve_number(control["max"], ctx, control_id, "max")
182.         if maximum <= 0:
183.             raise ValueError(f"Progressbar {control_id} must have a positive max")
184. 
185.         ratio = value / maximum
186.         display_ratio = min(1.0, max(0.0, ratio))
187.         kind = control.get("kind", "neutral")
188.         color = self.BAR_COLORS.get(kind, "#4ea1ff")
189.         thresholds = control.get("thresholds", {})
190.         if kind == "health":
191.             if ratio <= thresholds.get("critical", 0.15):
192.                 color = "#ff4d4d"
193.             elif ratio <= thresholds.get("warning", 0.35):
194.                 color = "#f0ad4e"
195.         elif kind == "capacity":
196.             if ratio >= thresholds.get("critical", 1.0):
197.                 color = "#ff4d4d"
198.             elif ratio >= thresholds.get("warning", 0.8):
199.                 color = "#f0ad4e"
200. 
201.         row = ctk.CTkFrame(parent, fg_color="transparent")
202.         row.pack(fill="x", pady=2)
203.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", control_id), ctx)
204.         text = f"{label}: {value:g}/{maximum:g}" if control.get("show_text", True) else label
205.         ctk.CTkLabel(row, text=text, width=150, anchor="w").pack(side="left")
206.         bar = ctk.CTkProgressBar(row, progress_color=color)
207.         bar.set(display_ratio)
208.         bar.pack(side="left", fill="x", expand=True, padx=(6, 0))
209. 
210.     def _add_list(self, parent, control, ctx):
211.         list_id = control["id"]
212.         label = control.get("label")
213.         rows = ctx.get(list_id, [])
214.         if label:
215.             ctk.CTkLabel(
216.                 parent,
217.                 text=self._fmt(label, ctx),
218.                 font=ctk.CTkFont(size=15, weight="bold"),
219.                 anchor="w",
220.             ).pack(anchor="w", pady=(6, 4))
221. 
222.         max_rows = control.get("max_rows")
223.         visible_rows = rows[:max_rows] if max_rows else rows
224.         for row in visible_rows:
225.             text = self._fmt(row.get("text", ""), ctx)
226.             action = row.get("action")
227.             enabled = row.get("enabled", True)
228.             if action and enabled:
229.                 ctk.CTkButton(
230.                     parent,
231.                     text=text,
232.                     command=lambda a=action: self._dispatch(a),
233.                     anchor="w",
234.                     height=32,
235.                 ).pack(fill="x", pady=2)
236.             else:
237.                 ctk.CTkLabel(
238.                     parent,
239.                     text=text,
240.                     anchor="w",
241.                     justify="left",
242.                     wraplength=900,
243.                 ).pack(fill="x", pady=2)
244. 
245.         if max_rows and len(rows) > max_rows:
246.             ctk.CTkLabel(
247.                 parent,
248.                 text=f"Showing {max_rows} of {len(rows)} entries; open detail to continue.",
249.                 text_color="#aaaaaa",
250.                 anchor="w",
251.             ).pack(fill="x", pady=4)
252. 
253.     def _add_button(self, parent, control, ctx):
254.         visible_if = control.get("visible_if")
255.         if visible_if and not ctx.get(visible_if):
256.             return
257.         label = self._fmt(control.get("label", ""), ctx)
258.         action = control.get("action")
259.         ctk.CTkButton(
260.             parent,
261.             text=label,
262.             command=(lambda a=action: self._dispatch(a)) if action else None,
263.             height=30,
264.         ).grid(
265.             row=self._action_index // self.ACTION_COLUMNS,
266.             column=self._action_index % self.ACTION_COLUMNS,
267.             sticky="ew",
268.             padx=3,
269.             pady=2,
270.         )
271.         self._action_index += 1
272. 
273.     def _render_control(self, parent, control, ctx, screen_id):
274.         control_type = control["type"]
275.         if control_type == "text":
276.             self._add_text(parent, control, ctx, title=control.get("variant") == "title")
277.         elif control_type == "input":
278.             self._add_input(parent, control, ctx)
279.         elif control_type == "progressbar":
280.             self._add_progressbar(parent, control, ctx)
281.         elif control_type == "list":
282.             self._add_list(parent, control, ctx)
283.         elif control_type == "button":
284.             self._add_button(parent, control, ctx)
285.         else:
286.             raise ValueError(
287.                 f"Unsupported control type {control_type!r} on screen {screen_id}"
288.             )
289. 
290.     def render(self):
291.         if self.frame is not None:
292.             self.frame.destroy()
293. 
294.         screen_id = self.controller.screen
295.         screen = self.screens.get(screen_id)
296.         if not screen:
297.             self.controller.screen = "front_page"
298.             screen = self.screens["front_page"]
299. 
300.         ctx = self.controller.get_context()
301.         containers, controls_by_frame, _definitions = self._frame_containers(screen)
302.         for frame_id in self.FRAME_ORDER:
303.             parent = containers.get(frame_id)
304.             if parent is None:
305.                 continue
306.             controls = controls_by_frame[frame_id]
307.             for control in controls:
308.                 self._render_control(parent, control, ctx, screen_id)
309. 
310. 
311. def main():
312.     root = ctk.CTk()
313.     DeclarativeGUI(root)
314.     root.mainloop()
315. 
316. 
317. if __name__ == "__main__":
318.     main()
